# Exact cap surplus and ordered-pair certificates from barycentric couplings

We reuse the accepted simultaneous barycentric coupling for arbitrary convex fibers and fixed positive weights. The contributions below are exact source budgets and cap-surplus identities, followed by an actual-geometry certificate that escapes the seven-fiber scalar-density obstruction. No universal anchor-selection theorem is asserted.

## 1. Reused multi-input coupling

Use accepted facts 793210f8a4be3647 and f6641f09c19819a3. For d>=1 and convex d-bodies K_j of volumes v_j>0 and weights lambda_j>0 summing to one, they provide one coupling X_j uniform on K_j such that Z=sum_j lambda_j X_j has density at most 1/B_lambda, where

    B_lambda=(sum_j lambda_j v_j^(1/d))^d,
    supp Z subset sum_j lambda_j K_j,
    E Z=sum_j lambda_j g_(K_j).

The coupling is fixed before the halfspace is chosen. Zero weights can be deleted. This is existing background; the distinct exact source-minus-output surplus and geometric certificates follow below.

## 2. Actual integer anchors, source budgets, and exact cap surplus

Let C subset R^n x R^d be a convex body with a finite set P of
positive-volume integer fibers K_z, and write v_z=|K_z|. Fix p in P.
An anchored hyperedge E consists of distinct bases z in P and positive
weights lambda_(E,z), summing to one, such that

    sum_(z in E) lambda_(E,z) z=p.

Convexity of C gives

    sum_(z in E) lambda_(E,z) K_z subset K_p.          (6)

Apply Section 1 to each edge. Its random tuple is denoted X_(E,z),
its weighted continuous barycenter Z_E, and its volume bound B_E.
Choose masses t_E>=0 and an own-fiber fraction 0<=s<=1 satisfying
the exact source constraints

    c_z:=s*1_(z=p)+sum_(E containing z)t_E/v_z <=1
                       for every z in P.             (7)

Set eta_E=t_E Law(Z_E) and eta=sum_E eta_E. Then

    eta_E <=(t_E/B_E)1_(K_p)dx,
    eta(K_p)=sum_E t_E,
    integral x d eta_E=t_E sum_(z in E)lambda_(E,z)g_z. (8)

There is no assertion that the barycenter in (8) equals the barycenter
of the unweighted source allocation. The source cost of an edge is
|E|t_E, not t_E and not sum lambda_(E,z)t_E. The lambda weights locate
its output; every endpoint marginal consumes mass t_E. Condition (7)
is essential even when hyperedges overlap.

Let H={ (z,x):a.z+u.x>=b } be any closed ambient halfspace. At each
sample of the E coupling its output margin is the weighted average
of its source margins. Thus, pointwise including equality statuses,

    I_(E,0):=1_H(p,Z_E) <= N_E:=sum_(z in E)1_H(z,X_(E,z)).

Define the nonnegative actual surplus

    Delta_E(H)=t_E E[N_E-I_(E,0)].                    (9)

Using every marginal exactly once gives the identity

    sum_(z in P)|K_z intersect H_z|
      =s|K_p intersect H_p|+eta(H_p)
       +sum_E Delta_E(H)
       +sum_(z in P)(1-c_z)|K_z intersect H_z|.       (10)

It holds for all oblique normals, pure integer normals, and closed
boundary fibers. There is no infimum interchange and no replacement
of a fiber sum by an integral over the integer projection. For nonzero
u the component measures have densities and give hyperplanes zero
mass; (10) does not need that fact to handle the indicator equality.

For example, with r=|E|>=2,

    N_E-I_(E,0) >= (2/r) sum_(z<w in E) I_(E,z)I_(E,w). (11)

Indeed for N_E=k>=1 the left side is at least k-1, and
k-1>=(2/r)binom(k,2). For k=0 both sides are zero.
The elementary estimate (11) must not replace the full surplus when
it loses relevant directional information.

Any barycenter of a nonzero positive measure supported on K_p is an
actual continuous point of K_p. In particular s1_(K_p)dx+c eta, with
c>0 and positive total mass, supplies a deterministic point there;
if s>0 it is interior. Choosing a coupling law or using random variables
in the proof does not make the final chosen point random. However,
this observation alone supplies no depth bound for that barycenter.
The archived seven-fiber obstruction is precisely a warning against
discarding (9), the separate measures in (8), and the unused terms
in (10) before choosing the point.

For d=0 the analogous statement is elementary with point masses:
every nonempty continuous fiber is the one point of R^0, barycenters
remain in the actual integer fiber, and (7),(9),(10) still hold with
counting measure. The root-volume density formula in Section 1 is not used with an undefined 1/d.
Nonparallel lower-dimensional positive intrinsic fibers are outside
the full-dimensional transport theorem above; no intrinsic extension
is claimed without its separate measure argument.

## 3. A non-scalar directional certificate for ordered pair centroids

The following uses actual component laws rather than their total
density ceiling. Let the anchor fiber be K_0 of volume k and centroid
g_0. Suppose we have distinct reflected pairs of integer bases
p-v_j,p+v_j, neither equal to p, whose two fibers are the SAME body
B_j, of volume b_j and centroid g_j. The shapes B_j may differ with j.
Assume for a nonzero continuous vector w that

    g_j=g_0+s_j w,
    0<s_1<=s_j for every j.                          (12)

Actual midpoint containment gives B_j subset K_0. The point
Y=(p,g_1) therefore belongs to S. Additional integer fibers are
allowed but not charged in the following lower bound.

Use the archived paired-centroid-tail theorem, in
`candidate 732b11a769399016`: for every
convex d-body B of centroid g, every u!=0, and every tau,

    |B intersect{u.(x-g)>=tau}|
      +|B intersect{u.(x-g)>=-tau}| >=2 Gamma_d |B|.   (13)

This is a proved ordinary theorem for every d>=1, with the interval
case included separately. If both thresholds in (13) are decreased
by the same nonnegative amount, the lower bound remains valid.

For a through-Y halfspace with nonzero continuous normal u, the
two thresholds in pair j relative to g_j have the form

    u.(g_1-g_j) +/- a.v_j.

If u.w>=0, (12) makes their common part nonpositive for every j.
Each pair consequently pays 2 Gamma_d b_j by (13). The own fiber
contains B_1, whose centroid is g_1, so it pays at least Gamma_d b_1
by ordinary Grunbaum. If u.w<=0, the own-fiber halfspace contains
g_0 and pays Gamma_d k; pair 1 still pays 2 Gamma_d b_1. At equality
u.w=0 both arguments are valid. Hence

    D_S(Y) >= Gamma_d min{k+2b_1, b_1+2 sum_j b_j}.   (14)

For a pure-integer through-Y halfspace, the own fiber is included and
at least one member of each reflected pair is included. Its mass is
at least k+sum b_j. This dominates the right side of (14), since
Gamma_d<=1/2 and b_1<=sum b_j. Moving a containing boundary parallel
to pass through Y can only decrease captured mass, so (14) holds for
every closed containing halfspace.

This certificate remembers the relative centroid positions, the fact
that identical pair laws satisfy (13) at all tilts, and an actual
contained own-fiber body. It does not follow from (k,T,L) alone.
The collinear ordering (12) is an explicit hypothesis, not an inferred
property of general compatible fibers.

## 4. The actual seven-fiber obstruction passes the richer certificate

Take the previously certified actual convex body with integer bases
z=-3,...,3 and fibers

    K_z=(1-|z|/4)T+(|z|/4)P,

where T is an area-one triangle of centroid zero and P one of its
vertices. Its construction and exact fibers are proved in
`candidate b04c74715df6cea2`.
The original mixed area is M=11/4. At p=0, the three identical
reflected pairs have

    (b_1,b_2,b_3)=(9/16,1/4,1/16),
    (g_1,g_2,g_3)=(P/4,P/2,3P/4),  k=1, g_0=0.

Thus (12) holds with w=P, and the single actual point Y=(0,P/4)
satisfies

    D_S(Y)>=Gamma_2 min{1+2(9/16), 9/16+2(7/8)}
           =(4/9)min{17/8,37/16}
           =17/18.                                 (15)

The requested OC raw target on this example is 11/18, so the exact
certified surplus is at least 1/3. This improves the previously saved
3/4 lower certificate at the same point. It does NOT claim that
17/18 is the exact depth. The scalar density-allocation envelope
remains bounded above by 136/225<11/18; no part of that audited
obstruction is contradicted, because the new argument retains data
that its definition deliberately discarded.

For binary padding [0,1]^(n-1) times this body, fix one binary base
block and the same point in it. Within that block every ambient
halfspace has exactly the one-dimensional integer offsets used above;
all other blocks only add nonnegative mass. Total mass is
2^(n-1)(11/4), so the OC raw target is still 11/18 and (15) still
certifies it for every n>=1.

The test uses only reflected two-input edges, because those already
expose what the old scalar compression loses. The proved multi-input
theorem additionally permits genuinely noncollinear anchored relations;
it is not falsely credited for the improvement in (15).

## 5. What remains to connect this to general OC

Equations (6)--(10) are a general transport accounting framework with
actual integer anchors, exact source capacities, and all-direction cap
surplus. They do not prove that an arbitrary body has an anchor and
allocation which pay its original total mass. In particular:

* Several outputs at different integer anchors cannot be treated as
  measures in one fictitious fiber.
* A source z used in several hyperedges consumes mass in every one,
  with the full constraints (7).
* A density ceiling cannot replace the component geometry if that
  replacement lands back in an archived failed scalar certificate.
* A family of random candidate points does not supply one deterministic
  center. Any eventual selection rule must name an actual p and y.

The next genuine arithmetic obligation is an anchor-selection/coverage
mechanism using (10) or a finite selected-critical-menu specialization
of it, while retaining the original denominator and obtaining exactly
2^(-n). The present proof makes that obligation explicit; it does not
hide it in a new allocation conjecture or infer it from the successful
seven-fiber calibration.
